newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia Telekom funds needs careful use-Yugo banks.
newsitem.headline: Serbia Telekom funds needs careful use-Yugo banks.

text.p: Yugoslavia's bankers called on the government on Tuesday to cautiously handle money raised from Serbia's Telekom company sale last week and asked not to be by-passed in the process of allocation of Telekom funds.

Bankers said almost one billion dollars collected after Serbia sold a 49-percent of stake in its Telekom Srbija to Italian and Greek companies Stet and OTE matched the country's M1 money supply and that any mishandling of funds could produce ill-effects.

"Telekom money matches our M1 money supply, and the government should cautiously plan how to spend it. Commercial banks can influence a rational distribution and spending of the Telekom money," Slobodan Vukovic, managing director of Prva Preduzetnicka Banka, told a bankers' meeting.

Borka Vucic, head of the largest Yugoslav banking group BB-Group and member of the Board of Directors of the Serbian Development Fund, the sole recepient of the Telekom money, said spending plans will be revealed within days.

The Serbian Development Fund will use the Telekom capital to finance exports, stimulate production growth and compensate lacking working capital, Vucic said at the Yugoslav Banking Association (YBA) Executive Board meeting.
"There are ideas to seek some firmer guarantees than simple bank guarantees, but in any case, commercial banks will not be left aside," Vucic said.
But economists have already cautioned the government not to allocate funds through the indebted banking sector before it restructures, consolidates and separates from big state loss-making companies.
Head of the brokerage house BEC Mirko Galjak insisted that such a substantial hard currency inflow will inevitably influence base money creation.

"Spending the Telekom money will be supervised by the government, but it cannot by-pass banks because base money creation will be changed. We do not know how the central bank will neutralise such an amount of cash which has arrived. It must prepare measures in advance," Galjak said.

Novica Medenica of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce Banking Committee said "with stability, EU trade perks and telekom money, the Yugoslav economy stands a chance for some progress. And the Telekom money will be available next week." -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
